 Arts and Culture Trial date set for Baby Reindeer court case
 By Jane Bradley Arts and culture correspondent
 Comment Published 16th Nov 2026, 14:41 GMT Richard Gadd and Jessica Gunning in Baby Reindeer. The hit Netflix show started out life on the Edinburgh Fringe. | Ed Miller/Netflix The court case is about a character in Baby Reindeer, which started out at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe
 The trial date has been set for a $170 million (£128m) law suit by a Scottish woman against streaming giant Netflix over the identity of a character in TV show Baby Reindeer .
 Fiona Harvey, from Glasgow, has claimed the character of Martha Scott in the series written and starred in by Fife-born Richard Gadd is based on her. She has accused Netflix of defamation and gross negligence.

Judge Robert Gary Klausner is to hear the claim brought by Ms Harvey against Netflix in front of a jury on 18 May next year, at the US District Court for the Central District of California. 
 Baby Reindeer started life at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe as a one-man stage show before being picked up by Netflix.
 Richard Gadd and Jessica Gunning in Baby Reindeer. The hit Netflix show started out life on the Edinburgh Fringe. | Ed Miller/Netflix Ms Harvey has previously denied stalking Mr Gadd and sending him 41,000 emails, hundreds of voice messages and 106 letters. 
 In September, the judge said there was a difference between Ms Harvey’s actions in real life and those of her character, saying those portrayed on the show were of a “worse degree”.
 He wrote: “There is a major difference between stalking and being convicted of stalking in a court of law.”
